series.source: Statistics Sweden (SCB), average monthly salary after sector, all sectors, total gender.
series.unit: SEK/month; annual comparator calculated as monthly × 12
series.definition: SCB average monthly salary across all sectors, both sexes (total gender), for each year 1992–2025. Salary is not disposable income or actual annual earnings.
series.transformation: Annual comparator is monthly average multiplied by 12; nominal values. Monthly source values retained in the separate salary file.

series.source: Sveriges Riksbank, Historical Monetary and Financial Statistics for Sweden, Volume I, Svante Prado workbook, Tables I.A10.1 and I.A10.2.
series.definition: Hourly earnings by manufacturing industry category and sex, plus a separately identified source-provided weighted average. Source table categories are represented in Swedish in the CSV.
series.coverage: Sweden; manufacturing workers. Coverage varies by industry and sex. Male categories are observed from 1860 or later depending on category; female coverage starts between 1865 and 1952 by category. Male weighted average 1871–2013; female weighted average 1921–2013.
series.transformation: Transcribed source observations without annualization or interpolation. Missing cells are omitted. This sectoral hourly series is not directly equivalent to all-sector monthly salary; overlap does not imply equivalent population or method.

series.source: Energimyndigheten, Energiläget i siffror 2026, Table 5.5, source note: SCB and Drivkraft Sverige; nominal values derived with SCB annual-average CPI.
series.definition: Annual average Swedish pump price for gasoline 95 octane (MK1/MK2), including taxes and VAT, as reported in Energimyndigheten table 5.5 in 2024 price level and converted back to nominal SEK. National annual series; product specification and fuel blend may vary over time.
series.coverage: Sweden, national annual average, 1980–2025. Separate pre-war reported price ranges are preserved in gasoline_historical_price_ranges.csv; they are tax-exclusive and not directly comparable with this series.
series.transformation: Calculated as source price in 2024 SEK × SCB annual-average CPI for observation year ÷ SCB annual-average CPI for 2024; rounded to öre. No interpolation.

series.source: Swedish Parliament, Första kammarens andra tillfälliga utskotts utlåtande nr 14 (1945), plus the 1948 official SOU and 1954 Government proposition for individual O-zone price observations.
series.unit: öre/liter; tax status specified per observation
series.definition: The 1925–1939 entries are the source's minimum and maximum retail-price quotations with gasoline tax excluded. The 1948 O-zone price is reported as 66 öre/liter with taxes; the 1953 O-zone figure is an October price calculation of 59 öre/liter with taxes. None of these points is a national annual mean or a consistent fuel specification.
series.coverage: Sweden, reported quotation ranges 1925–1939 plus individual O-zone observations in 1948 and 1953. There are no entries for 1940–1947, 1949–1952, or 1954–1979. The national annual pump-price series begins in 1980.
series.transformation: Transcribed min/max source values as öre per litre; where the source gives a point price, min equals max and the observation type identifies it. No averaging, tax adjustment, conversion to a single series, or interpolation.

series.source: Swedish Parliament and Government: historical radio licence values and radio/TV fee milestones from 1925 onward; SOU 2005:2 table of annual TV fees for 1991–2005; parliamentary statutory changes and reports for 2006–2018; parliamentary and Swedish Tax Agency values for the public service fee 2019–2025.
series.unit: SEK per year in force at 31 December; household (1991–2018), maximum per person (2019–2025)
series.definition: Annual radio and TV fee payable by one household with a TV receiver through 2018. From 2019, maximum individual public service fee, levied through income tax at 1 percent of taxable earned income up to a yearly cap. The fee type and liable unit changed on 2019-01-01.
series.coverage: Sweden, annual rates where the sources document a rate or a period at a fixed rate: radio licence from 1925; selected dated radio/TV fee rates through 1990; continuous annual rate series 1991–2025. Remaining gap in this dataset: 1967–1968. Newly documented coverage fills 1972–1987. Salary comparison is available for 1992–2025; historical hourly manufacturing wages are a separate population and unit. The series starts in 1925, when the public broadcast receiver licence began; earlier radio transmitter permits are a different fee and are not represented.
series.transformation: Records rate in force on 31 December where a dated transition is documented, not the amount actually paid during that calendar year. Annual values 1926–1950 and 1951–1955 use source statements that the rate was unchanged over those spans. 1956–1958 includes explicitly marked limited TV rollout/national coverage and radio-plus-TV fee; 1969 onward represents the household receiver fee, with color-TV supplement included where the source gives it. The 1972–1976 combined TV/radio receiver amount is 220 SEK general fee plus 100 SEK colour-TV surcharge; 1977 is 280 + 120 SEK, 1978–1979 is 340 + 140 SEK, and 1980 is 412 + 160 SEK; 1981–1982 it is 508 + 160 SEK; 1983 is 548 + 160 SEK and 1984 is 576 + 160 SEK; 1985 is 648 + 160 SEK; and 1986–1987 is 708 + 160 SEK. These yearly values follow the effective dates and unchanged periods documented in parliamentary/government materials. 1991–2018 is the household TV rate; 2019–2025 is the statutory individual maximum. Relative share is amount ÷ SCB average annual gross salary × 100 for En vuxen. Familj assumes two adults each earning SCB average: household rates counted once; individual maximum fees counted twice; denominator doubled. Trends are only calculated for adjacent years in the same documented regime; missing years remain gaps. No values are interpolated.

series.source: Energimyndigheten, Energiläget i siffror 2026, Table 5.5; source note in workbook: SCB and Drivkraft Sverige.
series.definition: Annual average pump price, gasoline 95 octane (MK1/MK2), including taxes and VAT, in 2024 price level.
series.transformation: Source values copied as published; this source-level file is retained separately from the derived nominal price file.

series.source: Statistics Sweden (SCB), Consumer Price Index (CPI), fixed index rebased to 2020=100, monthly observations aggregated to calendar-year arithmetic average.
series.definition: Annual arithmetic average of the 12 monthly fixed CPI index values. Rebased values preserve the year-to-year price-level ratio used for deflation/reflation.
series.transformation: Arithmetic mean of monthly values; CPI is used only to convert the gasoline series between 2024 prices and nominal annual SEK.

series.source: FZ.se's 2017 summary of Swedish new console prices, based on Cuponation's compilation from historical Swedish articles and forums including FZ, Aftonbladet and Sweclockers.
series.unit: nominal SEK per console/package at reported Swedish launch
series.definition: Reported Swedish new retail price at launch for Nintendo console models; discrete product launch observations, not calendar-year average retail prices. Switch 2 has no fixed official Swedish price; the recorded point is the console-only retail price reported at launch.
series.coverage: Sweden; nine observations: NES (reported as 1987, although Swedish retail availability began 1 September 1986), SNES 1992, Nintendo 64 1997, GameCube 2002, Wii 2006, Wii U Basic and Premium 2012, Switch 2017, and Switch 2 2025. The NES year/launch price are uncertain and marked; its displayed wage share uses the 1987 male weighted-average manufacturing hourly wage annualized at 2,080 hours, not the all-sector SCB salary series. Wii U is split into two launch packages per contemporary Swedish reporting. Wii is approximate; FZ reported about 2,700 SEK including VAT and one game on release day. Switch 2's 6,795 SEK is a reported Swedish retailer price for the console-only package; Swedish retailers set prices independently. FZ/Cuponation's 2017 compilation is secondary; see per-row source_url and price_basis in the data file.
series.transformation: Nominal reported Swedish launch prices transcribed from the cited sources. The Wii price is approximate and includes one game; Wii U Basic/Premium are separate packages. Switch 2 uses a contemporaneously reported retailer console-only price, not an official fixed Swedish price. For 1992 onward, wage share is launch price ÷ SCB all-sector average monthly salary for that year ÷ 12 × 100. For the NES source-year 1987 only, wage share is launch price ÷ male weighted-average manufacturing hourly wage from the Riksbank historical series ÷ 2,080 (40 hours × 52 weeks) × 100. That point uses a different population and is not directly comparable to SCB points. No inflation adjustment, no year-to-year trend arrow between distinct models.

series.source: Swedish Nintendo price observations from dated retail catalogues/advertisements (1987, 1991–1994), plus annual Swedish sales volumes and sales values by Nintendo platform from Dataspelsbranschen reports (1998–2015).
series.unit: Nominal SEK/game where documented; 2010–2015 nominal EUR/game only
series.definition: Nominal SEK per game. Two observation types are kept distinct: sparse arithmetic means of listed new-game prices in dated retailer advertisements/catalogues (not market means), and weighted average consumer expenditure per sold Nintendo software unit calculated by summing reported sales value and units across Nintendo platforms in Sweden. The annual reports cover physical game sales, exclude hardware and do not include digital sales.
series.coverage: Catalogue observations: 1987, 1991, 1992 (three samples), 1993 and 1994. Weighted Nintendo sales averages: each year 1998–2015. No verified catalogue price for 1988–1990 or 1995–1997; no comparable annual Nintendo unit/value dataset found for 2016–2026. Official-distributor brochure scans reviewed for 1988–1993 are game lists, not price lists. The 1990 Datormagazin examples at 398 SEK are in a hypothetical reader letter and are excluded. Current Tradera asking/listing prices indexed by original release year (for example Retrospel.nu) are second-hand market prices today, not original launch-year prices, and are excluded.
series.transformation: Catalogue sample means divide the sum of listed nominal retail prices by the count of priced titles; seller/platform/sample details are in each row. For 1998–2009, annual reported value (SEK) and units for all Nintendo platforms in Sweden were summed and divided; the 2009 report says distributor-to-retailer data were converted to estimated consumer expenditure including VAT and warns that they are not directly comparable with later GfK retail sell-through. For 2010–2015, reported Nintendo platform EUR values are summed and divided by reported units, retained only as EUR/game. Audit 2026-11-16 withdrew the previous conversion using annual-average EUR/SEK: 2010–2014 reports print point-date conversion rates, and 2015 does not establish the necessary SEK conversion basis. No SEK price, wage share or trend is published for these six observations. No inflation adjustment. Reported units are sample_size for these rows; catalogue rows use number of priced titles. Price shares use SCB all-sector mean monthly salary × 12 for 1992 onward; pre-1992 samples use the separately identified Riksbank male manufacturing hourly wage × 2,080 where available, which is not directly comparable. No interpolation; unobserved years remain gaps.
series.verification_limitations: Audit 2026-11-16: seven catalogue means cannot be fully independently recalculated because individual title-price transcriptions are absent; the 1992 issue 13 PDF URL returned 404. Retained values remain qualified source samples, not newly fully verified statistics. Historical report labels include Game Boy Advance in 2000, preceding hardware release; aggregate values follow the source as reported and do not establish platform release dates.

series.source: Nördliv, dated price statements in reviews explicitly identifying the tested Nintendo Switch / Switch 2 version; original quoted sources are Prisjakt, Nintendo/eShop and DekuDeals. These are secondary reported price observations, not transaction-level official statistics.
series.unit: nominal SEK/game; reported lowest price per title at the source-stated date
series.definition: Unweighted arithmetic mean per observation year of retained exact SEK lowest-price quotations for Nintendo Switch/Switch 2 games in Swedish reviews. Both Nintendo and third-party games, physical retail and digital eShop quotations. The sources do not separately document VAT per quote; no tax adjustment or foreign currency conversion is applied. Excludes hardware, accessories, subscriptions and add-ons.
series.coverage: Swedish review sample, each year 2017–2026 through retrieval date 2026-11-16; 61 retained title-price observations, 2–10 per year. No eligible observation found for 2016. This is neither a complete annual catalogue nor a sales-weighted or representative national annual price average. 2026 is incomplete and has no annual salary comparison.
series.transformation: Sum exact observed SEK amounts within year / count of titles, rounded to öre; computed by the pipeline from the individual observation CSV. Retain source URL, source-stated observation date, publication date, platform and exact price statement for every title. Inclusion: explicit tested Switch version; exact SEK amount; named price source; source-stated price date in publication year and no later than publication, at most 45 days before publication. Exclude approximate amounts, foreign currency, contradictory years/dates and prices explicitly for another platform. Yearly selection and channel mix vary, so no year-to-year trend is calculated. 2026 salary is missing, preserved as null; no extrapolation.
